title: They built a Temple…
paragraphs:
They built a Temple…
but it was never meant to hold God.

Because what happened in Jerusalem wasn’t just construction—
it was collision.

📖 In Genesis 22, a father walked up that mountain with trembling obedience.
Abraham carried the fire.
Isaac carried the wood.
And the question that split the silence:
That question didn’t just echo in the valley…
Because on that same region—Mount Moriah—God would answer it.

Not immediately.
Not cheaply.
But perfectly.

A king rises from dust to destiny.
David takes Jerusalem—not just as a capital, but as a calling.

Not the richest city.
Not the strongest.

Because God doesn’t look for impressive places—
He chooses strategic altars.

Jerusalem became the heartbeat of a nation…
but more than that—it became the meeting place between a holy God and a sinful people.
Built by Solomon, it stood as a visible declaration:
📖 “I have consecrated this house… My Name shall be there.” (1 Kings 9:3)

The Temple wasn’t proof that people were righteous.
It was proof that people were desperate.

Blood flowed.
Animals died.
Smoke rose.

Sin was covered.
But never completely removed.

The Temple was beautiful…
but it was also a warning.

You can stand in holy places—
and still carry an unholy heart.
You can sing, sacrifice, show up…

Not as a tourist.
Not as a spectator.
“Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up.”
was never meant to be a building.
It was always meant to be Him.

The Lamb that Isaac never became…
Jesus became.

The sacrifice that the Temple repeated daily…
Jesus finished in one moment.
📖 “The veil of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom.” (Matthew 27:51)
Because access was no longer earned…
It was chosen because it would carry:

🔥 The weight of sacrifice
👑 The authority of kingship
✝️ The power of redemption
But the story doesn’t end in a city…
Here’s the truth most people miss:

You don’t need to stand in Jerusalem
to meet God.

God stepped out of the Temple
and came running toward you.
Are you still trying to build your own temple?

Trying to earn your way in?
Trying to prove you’re enough?
Trying to cover what only Christ can cleanse?

The blood of animals covered sin.
The blood of Jesus erases it.
But to come to the One it was pointing to all along.

No distance.
No veil.
No delay.
Drop a 🔥 if you feel the weight of this truth.
“Behold, the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world!” (John 1:29)
We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
